name: Friday close
tasks: For a dozen counter payments, match the receipt and tip against the settlement in the bank export. Record discrepancies on the close sheet and sign it.
From twelve paper service slips, key the date, form ID, initials and ticked option into four columns. Reread each slip against the row to check the transcription.
Match twelve members' paid invoices against the individual deposits in the settlement file. List unmatched amounts for the treasurer and sign off.
Key the identifier, date, initials and cultivar from a dozen handwritten plant labels into the collection table. Compare each saved row with the physical label.
Implement a Python reconciler that joins receipts to bank settlements and unit-test duplicate amounts. Deliver the code; somebody else will perform this week's reconciliation.
The twelve slips are already a verified CSV. Run the existing import and compare its reported row count with twelve. No rekeying or reconciliation is needed.
Read a dozen signed paper waivers, transcribe the four marked fields into the intake table, then individually compare the saved values against the originals.
Give the shop lead a live spoken handover of this week's exceptions and answer their questions. The signed reconciliation sheet is already available.

name: Equipment handover
tasks: Use the existing inspector to align a reference WAV with an observed WAV. Step through both traces, locate the first two divergences and report offsets plus surrounding samples. Do not change the player.
Use the existing stream inspector to align a known-good byte trace with the new capture. Locate the first two mismatches and report their offsets with nearby values. The collector is already built.
Build and unit-test the stream inspector itself. Implement alignment and mismatch detection, package the CLI and hand it to the analysts. There are no captured streams to investigate yet.
Present a five-minute prerecorded demonstration of previously identified audio offsets. All offsets, slides and narration are supplied. Check the level and play the clip for the class.
Fit the new shoulder strap through two recessed buckles, trim the tails, melt the cut edges and load-test it with the recorder in the bag.
Thread its replacement webbing through two recessed buckles, trim and heat-seal the ends and check that neither buckle slips with a full carrier.
Run a five-minute pre-recorded clip during handover, using the provided speaking notes and existing slides. Check playback volume and introduce the clip.
